answer: Like a sonnet built on a strict meter, an agent economy can require every identity to post a basalt-solid stake before it may trade: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it is one of many sock-puppet copies. A shared terrace of reputation then lets honest agents vouch for newcomers only by risking their own stake, so a Sybil farmer must fund thousands of separate deposits and recruit real sponsors for each one. The attack stops being cheap spam and becomes an expensive, easily detected capital outlay, while a single honest agent pays only once.
